candidates.statement: This guidance is intended to assist trading partners in standardizing the data contained in the 30 product tracing information that trading partners must provide, capture, and maintain under 31 section 582. This guidance is also intended to help trading partners understand the data elements 32 that should be included in the product tracing information, particularly in situations where 33 trading partners are permitted by law to provide other trading partners with product tracing 34 information that omits certain elements that would otherwise be required. In addition, this 35 guidance recommends documentation practices that trading partners can use to satisfy the 36 product tracing requirements of section 582. This guidance does not address all provisions of the 37 DSCSA. As FDA works to implement other provisions of the DSCSA, the Agency expects to 38 issue additional guidance and/or regulations and conduct public meetings to further delineate the 39 requirements of the DSCSA. 40

candidates.statement: On November 27, 2013, the DSCSA was signed into law. Section 202 of the DSCSA, which 51 added new sections 581 and 582 to the FD&C Act, set forth new definitions and requirements 52 related to product tracing. Under section 582(b)(1), (c)(1), (d)(1), and (e)(1) of the FD&C Act, 53 trading partners are required to provide the subsequent purchaser 7 with product tracing 54 information for certain prescription drugs. Trading partners are required to capture and maintain 55 the applicable product tracing information for not less than 6 years after the date of the 56 transaction. 8 Trading partners are also required to provide applicable product tracing 57 information in response to a request from FDA or other appropriate Federal or State official in 58 the event of a recall or for the purpose of investigating a suspect or illegitimate product. 9

candidates.statement: This guidance is intended to assist trading partners in standardizing the product tracing 74 information that is captured, maintained, and provided to the subsequent purchaser, FDA, or 75 other appropriate State or Federal officials pursuant to the requirements under section 582 of the 76 FD&C Act. This guidance is also intended to help trading partners understand the data elements 77 that should be included in the product tracing information, particularly in situations where 78 trading partners are permitted by law to provide other trading partners with product tracing 79 information that omits certain elements that would otherwise be required. In addition, this 80 guidance recommends documentation practices that trading partners can use to satisfy the 81 product tracing requirements of section 582. Use of these recommendations will facilitate the 82 interoperable exchange of transaction information, transaction history, and transaction statements 83 between trading partners for each transaction involving a product pursuant to section 582(b)(1), 84 (c)(1), (d)(1), and (e)(1) of the FD&C Act. 85

candidates.statement: Licensed health care practitioners authorized to prescribe or administer medication under State 138 law, or other licensed individuals under the supervision or direction of such practitioners who 139 dispense or administer product in the usual course of their professional practice, are excepted 140 from the product tracing requirements that apply to dispensers under section 582(d)(1) and 141 (d)(5). 20 The trading partners of dispensers (including licensed health care practitioners that are 142 dispensers), however, must be authorized trading partners. 21

candidates.statement: Dispensers are required to maintain the product tracing information for a transaction for not less 147 than 6 years after the transaction. 22 Section 582(d)(1)(B) of the FD&C Act allows a dispenser to 148 enter into a written agreement with a third party, including an authorized wholesale distributor, 149 under which the third party confidentially maintains the product tracing information on the 150 dispenser’s behalf. FDA considers authorized trading partners and entities that are not 151 authorized trading partners to be acceptable third parties for this purpose. When such an 152 arrangement exists, the dispenser must maintain a copy of the written agreement. 23

candidates.statement: Wholesale distributors, dispensers, and repackagers generally must not accept ownership of a 171 product unless the previous owner provides the transaction information, transaction history, and 172 a transaction statement prior to, or at the time of, the transaction. 24 As required by section 173 582(a)(2)(A), FDA issued a draft guidance that established initial standards related to the 174 methods for the interoperable exchange of product tracing information. 25 In this guidance, we 175 provide recommendations for standardizing the product tracing information that trading partners 176 are required to exchange. Certain transactions that may involve the exchange of product tracing 177 information that is different from what is described in the statutory definitions of transaction 178 information, transaction history, or transaction statements are also addressed in this guidance. 179

candidates.statement: Manufacturers and repackagers that are creating the first transaction information for the product 215 they are introducing into commerce should use the strength and dosage form of the product as it 216 is written on the product label in the transaction information that they provide to subsequent 217 purchasers. Subsequent trading partners should use the strength and dosage form that is on the 218 transaction information they received from the product’s previous owner. The strength and 219 dosage form of the product should remain consistent in the documents for each transaction. 220

candidates.statement: The strength of the product that is provided in the transaction information should include the 224 amount of each API and the corresponding unit of measure (e.g., 500 mg). Units of measure 225 may be abbreviated (e.g., mg for milligram, mL for milliliter). For some products, the strength 226 may be expressed in the form of a concentration (e.g., 100 mg/mL), which is composed of the 227 amount of an API and its corresponding unit of measurement per unit of volume. Appendix C of 228 FDA’s Approved Drug Products With Therapeutic Equivalence Evaluations (commonly known 229 as the Orange Book) shows abbreviations used for strength at 230 https://www.fda.gov/downloads/drugs/developmentapprovalprocess/ucm071122.pdf . 231

candidates.statement: For the purposes of this guidance, a lot number is a set of alphanumeric characters that is 282 assigned by the manufacturer or repackager to identify a batch, or a specific identified portion of 283 a batch, that has uniform character and quality within specified limits. A manufacturer should 284 use the lot number it has assigned to the product in the transaction information that the 285 manufacturer provides to subsequent purchasers. If a repackager assigns a new lot number to the 286 product, the repackager should use the new lot number in the transaction information that it 287 provides to subsequent purchasers. In all other situations, a trading partner should use the lot 288 number that was on the transaction information it received from the product’s previous owner in 289 the transaction information that the trading partner provides to subsequent purchasers. If more 290 than one lot number is associated with the products received in a transaction, each lot number 291 should be reflected on the transaction information provided to the subsequent purchaser. 292 Alternatively, each lot number can be represented in separate transaction information provided to 293 the subsequent purchaser. 294

candidates.statement: For each transaction, the transaction information should remain separate from the transaction 337 history. The transaction history is defined in section 581(25) of the FD&C Act as a statement in 338 paper or electronic form, including the transaction information for each prior transaction going 339 back to the manufacturer of the product. In general, the transaction history for a product should 340 be a compilation of the transaction information for each prior transaction involving that product. 341 The recommendations in this section do not preclude a trading partner from providing more 342 information than is described. 343

candidates.statement: The transaction statement that a trading partner provides to a subsequent purchaser should 404 identify the trading partner as the entity transferring ownership and indicate that the trading 405 partner is in compliance with section 581(27)(A)-(G) of the FD&C Act.
